featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Gunjan
featured_reviews.review_text:
We were searching for Vada Pav at Chowpatty and found it at Karthik Snacks. The Vada Pav was simple yet delicious and definitely worth trying. The freshly made ginger tea was excellent—brewed right in front of us and very refreshing. We truly appreciated the effort and conveyed our thanks to the person who prepared it.

We also tried the Maska Bun and cherry bun. While they were decent, they didn’t quite match the high expectations set by the tea and Vada Pav. Another guest recommended the coffee as well, which we’ll try on our next visit.

Overall, Karthik Snacks is a great stop for snacks and tea, and I would definitely recommend guests to make a stopover here.

Right next door is Santosh Bhel Center, where we tried the Bhelpuri. It was really tasty and freshly prepared. What made the experience even better was the warm interaction with the people running the outlet—they were very nice to talk to and shared their experiences of running their stall and living in Mumbai away from home. A memorable and wholesome experience overall.

featured_reviews.name: Kunal Singh
featured_reviews.review_text: The food stalls at Juhu Beach offer a quintessential Mumbai street food experience that is as flavorful as it is chaotic, serving up iconic dishes that define the city's culinary spirit. The dedicated food court area is a sensory overload of sizzling Tawa Pulao, buttery Pav Bhaji, and tangy Panipuri, all prepared at a frantic pace to feed the massive crowds. While the taste is often undeniably delicious and hits the spicy notes perfectly—especially the refreshing Kala Khatta Golas—the hygiene standards can be a major concern for the cautious eater, given the surrounding environment. It remains a "must-visit" for the adventurous foodie willing to overlook the grime and crowds for a bite of authentic, greasy, and spicy local fare.

Visited Street and Spice Kitchen in Juhu recently, and it turned out to be a great budget-friendly option for pure vegetarian food.

The menu is limited, but whatever they serve is definitely worth trying. We started with their Chole, which tasted very authentic and flavorful—truly satisfying from the first bite.

Next, we had the Aloo Cheese Paratha, which was well-stuffed with spiced potatoes and cheese, and served with Dal Makhni. The combination was delicious and quite filling.

Overall, a great spot in Juhu for tasty and affordable veg food. Definitely recommended for vegetarian food lovers!

featured_reviews.name: The Beekeeper
featured_reviews.review_text:
In a nutshell, the only reason this place seems to be surviving is because it’s probably the only snack vendor on that side of Juhu Beach. Otherwise, it’s honestly not worth the effort.

The first issue was the service. The staff at the stall were quite rude and the place seemed poorly managed. I placed an order and waited for around 15 minutes. When I went back to check on it, the server casually said that I had never ordered. I had to explain my order to them again — something I had already repeated three times earlier. What made this more surprising was that there were hardly a few other customers, so it wasn’t even a busy situation.

Secondly, the food quality was disappointing. We ordered Pav Bhaji but it didn’t taste good at all. The bhaji was quite bland and the pav was hard, which made it feel like the food wasn’t fresh.

Lastly, considering the service, food quality, and preparation, the prices felt quite high for what was being offered.

Overall, the experience was not great. I would honestly suggest saving your money (and possibly your health) and trying other options instead.

Why is Nandu Dosas the best place in Mumbai to have dosas?

We all know that there are 100s of best places in Mumbai for dosas, but this one is beyond the best. It is simply so fine and tasty that even the best places seem dull in front of it. The place we are talking about is Nandu Dosa, located behind Ritumbara College, Vile Parle.

Read below to find out what makes Nandu Dosa one of the best dosa places in Mumbai.

Sizzling Cheese Jinni Dosa
Nandu Dosa is famous for its Jinni Cheese Dosa, which is crispy in nature, stuffed with vegetables such as carrots, cabbage, and capsicum, adding spiciness and sweetness to the tangy, rich Schezwan sauce.
Bet it’s so tasty that you would order another one as you cannot resist its saucy nature and cheese-filled goodness.

Made with Fresh Batter
Nandu dosas are fresh in nature because the batter itself is made early in the morning, preserving its freshness for the whole day so that it doesn’t get spoiled.
If you try the idli as well, it still holds the freshness which feels like it was recently made — so yum, so tasty.

Its Famous Red Chutney
So sweet, so spicy — just tasting like a wow!
Yes, Nandu’s orange chutney is an absolute wow, made with cheese and chutney which has a sweet and spicy taste. Filled with red chili, tamarind, and roasted chana dal, it adds a perfect blend to the Jinni dosas.

Pro Tip
If you have an angry girlfriend and want to make her happy, take her to Nandu Dosas and order the Cheese Jinni Dosa.
See how her anger melts from anguish to just like the sweet orange chutney. This is one of the best ways to make her heart go from "hmm" to "uhmmm".

Nandu Dosas has a variety of dosas, but I would highly recommend trying the Jinni Dosa and Paneer Mysore Dosa, as these are the best-selling options and are always in high demand. They carry the authentic taste of South India while adding more variations to the South Indian culinary experience.

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Sagar Chinese located at N S Rd No. 10, opposite Sukhmani Society, JVPD Scheme, Juhu — and honestly, it was such a satisfying experience! This spot is known to be a favourite of Kartik Aaryan, and after trying the food, we can totally understand why.

It’s a small, simple restaurant, but don’t judge it by its size — the Chinese cuisine here is absolutely amazing and full of flavour. Perfect for late-night cravings in Juhu!

Here’s what we tried:

• Chicken Lollypop Masala – Properly masaledar, nostalgic vibes, and super tasty. One of our favourites!
• Crispy Chicken – Perfectly crunchy on the outside, juicy inside. Fresh and delicious.
• Hunan Chicken (Dry) – Bold flavours, slightly spicy, and extremely satisfying. A must-try!
• Chicken Triple Schezwan Fried Rice – Total game changer! Fully loaded, spicy, saucy, and easily the star of the meal.

The service and management were smooth and quick despite the rush. Staff was polite and the food arrived on time.

Overall, if you’re in Juhu and craving authentic, street-style Chinese — especially late at night — this place definitely deserves to be on your list. Affordable, tasty, and totally worth it! 🍜🔥

Together, they’ve earned quite a name for serving some of the best Indo-Chinese food in the Juhu–Andheri belt.

The food here packs bold flavours and generous portions — truly great value for money when you compare the quality and quantity. Their Manchow Soup, Chicken Crispy, and Triple Rice are absolute must-tries — each dish has that perfect street-style punch that keeps you coming back for more.

That said, the service is a real weak spot. It’s slow and needs serious improvement. A bit more attention to service would easily make this place a complete winner.

featured_reviews.name: Rishikesh Verma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Imlee – The Chaat Gali offers a modern twist on traditional Indian street food in the heart of Bandra. The ambiance is chic and inviting, providing a comfortable setting for chaat enthusiasts.  ￼

Food:
The menu showcases a variety of regional chaats, including Pani Puri, Bhel Puri, and Aloo Tikki, each prepared with a contemporary flair. While the use of fresh ingredients is evident, some dishes might benefit from bolder flavors to capture the authentic street food essence.  ￼

Service:
The staff is attentive and ensures a pleasant dining experience. However, during peak hours, service can be slightly delayed due to high demand.

Value for Money:
Considering the upscale ambiance and quality ingredients, the pricing is reasonable. It’s a great spot for those looking to enjoy street food in a more refined environment. ￼

Overall Experience:
Imlee is a commendable attempt to elevate traditional chaats for a modern audience. While there’s room for enhancing the authenticity of flavors, it’s worth a visit for those seeking a unique chaat experience in Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Noel Rodriques
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you love street food, Imlee - The Chaat Galli is a must-visit! 🌟
Their Pani Puri cart is magic — imagine tasting Delhi ke Golgappe, Kolkata ke Puchka, and Mumbai ki Pani Puri all at one place! Each one was fresh, crispy, and full of flavour.h

We also tried their Dahi Bhalle and Papdi Chaat — both were loaded with dahi and perfectly balanced masalas. The Cheese Pav Bhaji was rich, creamy, and super satisfying.

And to end on a sweet note — the Meerut ki Jalebi totally stole the show! Crispy, juicy, and just the right amount of sweetness.

The place has a lovely ambiance where you can actually sit and enjoy your street food cravings in comfort. Highly recommend this spot for chaat lovers in the city!

✅ Tip: Don’t miss the Pani Puri cart experience — it’s fun and delicious!

featured_reviews.name: Sneha
featured_reviews.review_text:
At Imlee, Santacruz, we recently tried a few things. We started with three varieties of everyon’s favourite - Panipuri, Golgappa and Puchka. Then we had Dilli ki famous Rani Kachori Chaat which was highly recommended by Curly Tales. Honestly, I had never eaten this inspite of many trips to Delhi.  Then we had Agra ke Matar Poori our Kacche Tamatar ki Sabji.
Kadhi Chawal from Haridwar ki Gali was another staff recommendation. This kinda took me back to the Kadhi chawal from Chotiwala in Rishikesh. Simple and perfect!
We finished our meal with Ras Malai.
There were many more items on the menu. All regional street food from North and Central India. Everything we ate here left us wanting more. The staff’s recommendations were on point. This is Imlee by Neeti Goel & Curly Tales, a cute place where you have your favourite street food under one roof. Check it out.

featured_reviews.name: abhishek nair
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Chaat Lover’s Paradise!

Visited Imlee with my fiancé and absolutely loved it! The ambiance and vibe were great, and the variety of chaats from across India was impressive. We tried pani puri, pav bhaji, puchka, chole bhature, and rani kachori—all were full of authentic flavors. A must-visit for anyone craving delicious Indian street food!

featured_reviews.name: Komal Jaisingh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried the newly opened Imlee at Santacruz and loved the whole experience!
Their menu brings together iconic flavors from Mathura, Agra, Indore, Rajasthan, Amritsar, Delhi, and Mumbai—each dish felt like a little journey across India.
From spicy pani puri to rich paneer chole bhature and the dreamy Jodhpuri gulab jamun, every bite was full of authentic, homely goodness.
A must-visit if you're craving soulful, desi comfort food with a regional twist!

featured_reviews.name: Rohit Upadhyay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Imlee Chaat Gali in Santacruz West is a total flavour bomb! If you’re someone who lives for street-style food but also loves a great vibe and ambience, this place is going to win your heart.

Every dish I tried was lipsmacking and delicious—from the tangy chaats to spicy snacks, the flavors are just spot-on. It’s like the best of Indian streets served up in a trendy, clean, and super fun setting. 😋✨

What really stood out? The ambience. It’s not just a restaurant, it’s an experience. Think colorful, energetic, and full of character—perfect for catching up with friends, clicking some aesthetic pics, or simply enjoying great food with a side of great vibes.

This place nails the balance between authentic street food charm and modern restaurant comfort. Will 100% be back to explore more from their menu!

featured_reviews.name: juhi roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of Indian street food but want to enjoy it in a clean, comfy setting with lovely vibes — Imlee by Chaat gali  is a must-visit!

I went with my family and absolutely loved the experience. From the fun twist of three flavours of Panipuri to the comforting Jodhpur pyaaz kachori, everything was full of flavour and nostalgia.

We also tried the Amritsari chole bhature, Rani Kachori Chaat, and the super refreshing Vrindavan-style lassi served in kulhad — all spot on. And the Meerut-style jalebi with rabdi? Ended the meal on such a sweet note!

The ambiance is beautiful and staff is really warm — perfect for a family outing or a chill meal with friends. Highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: Bhumika Shanbhag

This can officially be termed as a total chaat-lover's paradise! The place has a vibrant vibe, and the food just hits the chatpata spot.

featured_reviews.name: Nikita
featured_reviews.review_text:
We were excited to try some authentic North-Eastern food and were pleasantly surprised by how good it tasted. The menu offered a nice range of vegetarian options, which was impressive since most North-Eastern meals tend to include fish or meat. We ordered the Manipuri and Nepali thalis. Both were flavorful, well-prepared, and gave a genuine taste of the region.

Unfortunately, the experience was let down by the service. Our food took almost an hour to arrive, and despite asking multiple times, each server assured us it would be ready in “10 minutes”, which wasn’t true. No one came by to apologise for the delay, and it felt like the staff just didn’t care.

Even though the food itself was excellent, the poor service overshadowed everything. Sadly, we wouldn’t return, which is a pity given how delicious the dishes were.

featured_reviews.name: Abhinay Junghare

featured_reviews.name: Yi Ping Bong
featured_reviews.review_text: What an utterly underrated place serving a myriad of northeastern flavours! Our group had a fun time sampling the different thalis from Assam, Nepal, Manipur and Naga. I ordered the smoked pork manipuri thali, which awakened my senses (and sinus) with each tiny bowl bursting with flavors that surprises with each taste. Food took awhile to reach us since we placed 6 thali orders in one shot but boy was it worth it. Even the fried chicken appetizer was delicious with its umami bomb of a batter.

featured_reviews.name: J S
featured_reviews.review_text:
For a person very new to north eastern cuisine this was one of the most interesting restaurants I have been to. It is a tiny place with a few but comfortable tables and a good overall ambience.

Highly excited about the food we dove right into ordering the appetizers and soup.

First one to come was their prawns thupka soup - which was perfection. Flavourful broth, nice firm noodles just what was needed.

Next was pork momos which was served with a small pork soup. The momos had nicely flavoured meat in adequate quantity and with the soup were just so flavourful.

The next two dishes to come were the pork ribs and chicken wings from their specials part of the menu. The first two bites revealed a ton of smoky flavours but then the spice kicked in, which we eventually discovered was from bhoot jhalokia peppers. We powered through them teary eyed, loved the experience but can't say will try it again. But if spicy food is your domain, I would say you must try it.

The mains were a curry with fermented bamboo and pork and plain rice and also a portion of pork fried rice. We absolutely loved the pork fried rice. The curry had a flavour which was new and unique to us and some of us liked it while others did not.

The dessert was a red / purple rice kheer.. but it was really disappointing.

The service is friendly and acceptable.

Will go back to try more things on their menu without the bhoot jhalokia.😀

featured_reviews.name: Prathamesh Bhosale
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Had an amazing experience at Chaat Hauz in Khar! As someone who loves chaat, it's rare to find a place that gets every dish right, but this place absolutely delivered.
We started with the Palak Patta Chaat, and it was outstanding. The crispy spinach leaves, perfectly balanced chutneys, and crunchy toppings created an explosion of flavors and textures in every bite. Easily one of the best versions I've had in Mumbai.
The Ragda Pattice was equally impressive. The pattice was crisp on the outside and soft inside, while the ragda was flavorful and comforting without being overly spicy. It had that authentic street-food taste with a premium touch.
The Dahi Makhana Chaat was a pleasant surprise and probably the most unique dish of the lot. Light, refreshing, and beautifully balanced with creamy dahi and flavorful chutneys, it stood out from the usual chaat options available elsewhere.
The star of the evening was the Avocado Papdi Chaat. Such a creative fusion dish! The creamy avocado blended beautifully with the traditional chaat elements, creating something innovative without losing the essence of authentic Indian chaat.
The presentation of every dish was excellent, ingredients tasted fresh, portions were satisfying, and the service was warm and attentive. The restaurant has managed to give traditional chaat a modern twist while maintaining authentic flavors.
If you're a chaat lover looking for something beyond the ordinary, Chaat Hauz in Khar is definitely worth visiting. Every dish we tried was packed with flavor, creativity, and quality. Looking forward to coming back and exploring more of their menu. Highly recommended! 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

featured_reviews.name: Zakiya Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: QFinally found the best chaat spot in Khar and Chaat Hauz completely lives up to the hype — every single item is a flavour bomb and you can taste the freshness in every bite. Started with their legendary pani puri where the puris were perfectly crisp and the teekha-khatta pudina pani had that perfect street-style kick that hits instantly, then moved to dahi batata puri which was insanely balanced with chilled sweet dahi, tangy chutneys, and aloo masala that just melts in your mouth without making the puri soggy at all. The sev puri had great crunch with fresh onion-tomato toppings and the ragda pattice was piping hot with buttery ragda, spicy chutneys, and loads of sev on top — proper Mumbai style. Even though it’s a small standing/takeaway setup with no seating, the counters are surprisingly clean, staff is super quick even during the 6-9pm rush, and hygiene is clearly a priority which is rare for street chaat places. Prices are very reasonable at ₹60-120 per plate and portions are generous, plus the bhaiya serving is polite and remembers regulars. If you’re craving authentic, no-nonsense Mumbai chaat that tastes exactly like it should, skip the fancy cafes and come straight here — Chaat Hauz is a Khar institution for a reason and I’m already planning my next visit for bhel and samosa chaat!

featured_reviews.name: Yash Mistry
featured_reviews.review_text: One8 Commune Juhu really delivers on both food and aesthetics. We tried a few of the signature dishes and everything was plated beautifully and tasted fresh. The menu has a great variety, and the drinks menu is just as impressive. It’s a bit on the premium side, but the quality of the food and the overall experience make it worth it for a special occasion.

featured_reviews.name: Priyank
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had dinner at One8 Commune in Mumbai last night and had a really nice time overall. We tried the Chicken Dimsum, Burrata Cheese Chicken Spaghetti, Patata, a Chicken Rice Bowl, and a mocktail. The taste was good, well-seasoned, fresh, and nicely plated.

The ambience is warm and cozy, perfect for a one time dinner or a casual date. Our total bill came to around Rs 4,000, and while everything tasted good, the portion sizes felt a bit small for the price, so yes, it’s on the expensive side.

One important thing to note: they strictly follow a “shoes mandatory” rule, so don’t show up in slippers/sandals expecting to enter.

Overall, if you’re looking for a premium dining experience in Mumbai with great vibes and good food, One8 Commune is worth trying, just be ready for the pricing and portions.

featured_reviews.name: Soniya Shrestha
featured_reviews.review_text:
First time in Mumbai and honestly a little confused at first, hopping from one place to another and somehow ending up here. But I’m actually glad I did.
Such a lovely place and restaurant. Good service, kind staff, and really good food. What surprised me the most was the price very reasonable. Many celebrity restaurants tend to be overly expensive, but this one felt just right.
And the best part… I love the number 8, so that made it even more special. ✨

featured_reviews.name: Vrushti Chheda
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited One8 commune at the end of Jan, ordered dimsum, pizza etc. The food was okayish. Service was good but not that good as compared to other cafes I have visited till now. But the Ambience was 10/10 no doubt. Overall experience was good

featured_reviews.name: Chandni Sahgal
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place serves multicuisine food and there is no theme. So there is something for every taste!
Since it is housed in Kishore Kumar's Bunglow, I had imagined my Bollywood Vibe.
Or cricket....
Cocktalis were nice, starters quite generic.

featured_reviews.name: Musheb Amroliwala
featured_reviews.review_text: Me and my family enjoyed here very much. Food was top notch and so was service and ambience. The manager was very courteous to give us complimentary dessert as we had to change our table. Definitely will visit here again.

featured_reviews.name: prasanjit devnath
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a wonderful experience at One8 Commune. The ambiance is stylish, warm, and welcoming, making it a perfect place to relax with friends or family. The food was impressive — especially the Mushroom Googly Dimsums and the mains, which were packed with flavour and beautifully presented.

The staff was courteous and attentive, ensuring we had a smooth dining experience. Prices are slightly on the higher side, but the overall quality, ambience, and service make it worth it.

Highly recommended for a memorable dining experience or a special evening out!

featured_reviews.name: dylan hira
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited One8 Commune, Juhu on the 29th of December with our cricket club from London and our supporters for a social dinner and drinks after a match we played in Mumbai as part of our tour. The entire event was pre-organised via WhatsApp with Nitesh, who was incredibly helpful, professional, and responsive throughout the whole planning process.

On the day itself, Tushar and Raj made sure everything was perfectly set up and ran smoothly from start to finish. We had a private area, and the ambience, food, and drinks service were all absolutely spot on. There honestly isn’t a single fault we could find — the food was outstanding, and a few of the lads even said the starters were the best they’ve had on the entire tour.

An excellent venue with fantastic staff and top-quality food and service. Highly recommended for group events and social gatherings.

featured_reviews.name: Soham Railkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The moment you bite into Samrat’s batata vada, time slows. The golden crust crackles like a whispered secret, giving way to a silken, spiced potato filling that melts on your tongue and swirls around your senses like a warm monsoon breeze. There’s a flirtation of garlic, a teasing kiss of green chili, and just when you think it’s over, the dry chutney layered in the pav leaves a smoky, lingering memory on your lips.

It’s not just street food—it’s seduction served hot, crisp, and unapologetically Indian.

You don’t just eat Samrat’s batata vada.
You close your eyes.
You feel it.
And you remember it long after the last crumb is gone.

Its good for a quick bite... a fill in brunch.. or early evening snack.

If you’re craving authentic South Indian comfort food in Juhu, Shiv Sagar does not disappoint. The Benne Dosa was perfectly crisp on the outside, soft inside, and generously coated with butter—exactly how it should be. Rich, flavourful, and absolutely satisfying.
The Thatte  Idli was equally impressive soft, fluffy, and light, served fresh and hot. Paired with their delicious coconut chutney and flavourful sambar, it made for a truly wholesome meal.
Service was quick, the place was clean, and the food quality was consistent. Definitely a reliable spot for South Indian food lovers. Will surely visit again! 😊

featured_reviews.name: Shiv
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience during my recent visit. While dining, I discovered a cockroach in the food that was served to me. This is completely unacceptable and raises serious concerns about hygiene and cleanliness standards in the kitchen.
Finding an insect in a meal is not only unpleasant but also a major health hazard. It made the entire dining experience distressing, and I lost all confidence in consuming anything further from this establishment.
Cleanliness should be the top priority for any place that serves food, and I sincerely hope the
management takes immediate action to improve their sanitation practices. Until then, I cannot recommend this restaurant to anyone who values food safety.

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Lube Cafe Veg & Jain offers a good dining experience with delicious food, but the overall ambiance felt a bit off. The vibe wasn’t very welcoming or comfortable, and the indoor smell was slightly unpleasant, which made us feel uneasy. However, the food quality made up for it – we tried the Chilli Paneer and Cold Coffee, both of which were excellent.

The cafe features private seating spaces for two, adding a unique touch. A major highlight is that it is 100% vegetarian and offers Jain food options, making it a great choice for those with dietary preferences. It’s advisable to book a table through the District app to avail discounts. While the ambiance may not have worked for us, it could be a different experience for others—worth trying at least once!
